name: day-71-simt-execution-plan
statement: Declared inputs for an analytical SIMT execution-model report. Hardware values are copied from the cited NVIDIA sources; latencies, register budgets, and kernel byte and FLOP counts are labeled planning inputs. No GPU, CUDA kernel, or latency was executed or measured.

sources: NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide v12.6 (archive 12.6.3), Table 21 Technical Specifications per Compute Capability, and Table 4 (64 FP32 add/multiply/multiply-add results per clock per SM for 7.x and 8.0)

vector_add.basis: c[i] = a[i] + b[i] over 2^24 float32 elements: one add, two 4-byte reads, and one 4-byte write per element. 16 registers per thread is a declared budget, not a compiler result; every budget from 1 to 32 gives the same occupancy for 256-thread blocks on these devices.

rgb_to_grayscale.basis: Interleaved 8-bit RGB in and one 8-bit luma value out per pixel, counting three weighted channel products and two adds; the register budget is declared, not compiled.

occupancy_sweep.basis: Declared sweep points with no shared memory beyond the driver reservation; 255 is the guide's per-thread register maximum.

memory_latency.basis: The CUDA guide (section 5.2.3) says off-chip memory latency is typically hundreds of clock cycles; 400 and 800 SM cycles are declared sensitivity points in that range, not measured or device-specific latencies. Rows are evaluated at each SM's maximum resident warps.

arithmetic_latency.basis: The CUDA guide (section 5.2.3) states a typical 4-cycle latency for most arithmetic instructions only for compute capability 7.x, so compute capability 8.0 is not tabulated.

wave_quantization.basis: A fixed grid of 1,024 blocks, for example a 32 x 32 grid of output tiles, with a declared 64-register budget.

sources: NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide v12.6 (archive 12.6.3), section 5.2.3 Multiprocessor Level: most arithmetic instructions take typically 4 cycles on 7.x, so 4 schedulers need 16 warps; off-chip latency is typically hundreds of clock cycles
NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide v12.6, section 5.3.2 Device Memory Accesses: global memory instructions move 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16-byte words
NVIDIA CUDA C++ Programming Guide v12.6, sections 2.2 Thread Hierarchy and 4.1 SIMT Architecture: a 2D thread ID is x + y * Dx and warps hold consecutive thread IDs starting at thread 0
NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit 12.6 cuda_occupancy.h, cudaOccMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor: warp, register, shared memory and block limits per SM
